issue.title: [GelfTcpTransport] Connection failed: executor not accepting a task error

repository.name: gelfclient
repository.description: GELF client library for Java based on Netty 4

issue.body:
When I tried to initialize a gelf transport and send some logs to gelf tcp input, it throw the error "[GelfTcpTransport] Connection failed: executor not accepting a task ". It seems to be threw by  netty but I cannot locate where it threw. 

What is the reason it may be caused by? How to solve it?

body: We still see this issue in 4.1.33. Any updates on this ?
@james-r-smith this means you already shutdown the `EventLoopGroup`.

@normanmaurer, okay. So, where I see it happening is when I successfully connect, which then calls `reconnectOnClose(future);` in `ReconnectListener`. So, I notice now that my method tries to reconnect on close `bootstrap.connect().addListener(this);`. This could be a problem when the `EventLoopGroup` is already closed. Makes sense. Any way I can do a check on the `EventLoopGroup` within that lambda?

**EDIT**: I just put some logs within that section, and it's not shutdown at that point, but it is in the middle of shutting down, which leads to it not accepting tasks. I don't want to have if statements for all three `EventLoopGroup` states. Is it safe to just check `bootstrap.config().group().isShuttingDown()` for all cases? Any tips on checking whether to reschedule a connection without having the exception would help a ton. Thanks!
